posts.title: 말씀 카드: 지쳤을 때
posts.caption:
Running on empty?

“Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.” Matthew 11:28

From the WithGod app’s note on this verse (written with AI):
Jesus speaks these words to a crowd worn down by daily work and by the heavy demands of religious rules, so the invitation comes before anything is fixed. He does not tell the tired to first sort themselves out; he calls them to come just as they are. The word "labor" points to effort that has been kept up for a long time, while "heavily burdened" suggests a weight too much to carry alone. Nothing in this call asks you to pretend you are fine. Today, you can bring your tiredness to him as it is, without putting on a brave face first.

Send this to someone who’s been carrying a lot lately.

posts.title: 캐러셀: 외로울 때
posts.caption:
When you feel alone, even in a full room.

Five verses for the lonely days: Psalm 25:16, Deuteronomy 31:8, Psalm 27:10, Psalm 139:9–10 and John 14:18.

The first one is a prayer from someone who felt the same way, three thousand years ago.

Send this to someone who might be feeling it today.

#bibleverse #dailybibleverse #scripture #faith #loneliness
alts: When you feel alone (title card)
Bible verse card. You’re not the first to feel this: “Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted.” Psalm 25:16 (World English Bible).

Bible verse card. When you’re facing it by yourself: “The LORD himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.” Deuteronomy 31:8 (World English Bible).
Bible verse card. When the people closest let you down: “When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.” Psalm 27:10 (World English Bible).

Bible verse card. When you’re far from home: “If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea, even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me.” Psalm 139:9–10 (World English Bible).
Bible verse card. When you feel left behind: “I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.” John 14:18 (World English Bible).
Feeling it today? Tell WithGod what it’s like. It finds the verse for that. Link in bio. Send this to someone who might need it.

posts.title: 말씀 카드: 두려울 때
posts.caption:
For the days fear gets the first word.

“Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.” Isaiah 41:10

From the WithGod app’s note on this verse (written with AI):
Isaiah spoke these words to Israel when it felt small and afraid among the great powers of the ancient world, and God answered with promise after promise: I am with you, I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you. Each sentence has the same subject, God, so the weight of the promise rests on him rather than on how steady you feel. The image of the right hand, the strongest one, shows a hold that does not depend on your grip. Today, when your own strength to hang on runs thin, you can remember that the one holding you has not let go.

Save this for the next time fear gets loud. A new verse here every morning.

#bibleverse #dailybibleverse #scripture #faith #encouragement

posts.title: 대표 캐러셀: 잠 못 드는 밤 (고정)
posts.caption:
For the nights your mind won’t slow down.

Five verses for when the worries follow you to bed: Philippians 4:6–7, 1 Peter 5:7, Psalm 127:2, Psalm 4:8 and Psalm 3:5.

You don’t have to solve everything before you sleep tonight.

Save this for a restless night, and send it to someone who’s still awake.

#bibleverse #dailybibleverse #scripture #faith #peace
alts: For the nights your mind won’t slow down (title card)

Bible verse card. When your thoughts keep racing: “In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.” Philippians 4:6–7 (World English Bible).
Bible verse card. When it’s too much to carry: “Casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.” 1 Peter 5:7 (World English Bible).

Bible verse card. When you can’t stop working it out: “It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.” Psalm 127:2 (World English Bible).
Bible verse card. When you finally lie down: “In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety.” Psalm 4:8 (World English Bible).
Bible verse card. For the morning after: “I laid myself down and slept. I awakened, for the LORD sustains me.” Psalm 3:5 (World English Bible).
Still awake? Tell WithGod what’s keeping you up. It finds the verse for that. Link in bio. Save this for a restless night.
